method.features: Band-pass both inputs at 250–3800 Hz, remove local weighted DC and measure 240 ms Hann-window normalized correlation and signed least-squares reference gain at 80 ms hops. Limit analysis to reference windows at or above 25 percent of its 80th percentile RMS. Normalize each cue by its 70th percentile among those windows. Require reference support in at least 36 windows and broad positive matching; unrelated or same-words re-recorded reference declines.
method.input: Compare the same six-second mono recording on an equal 16 kHz clock using an earlier copy as a separate input. The earlier recording carries +5 dB interfering speech. The submitted recording carries 0, -5, or -10 dB with a different AMI meeting in each role and pair. There is no attempt to align arbitrary recordings or infer a new clock.
method.localization: Measure a local deficit with the median over each nine-window sequence, requiring at least six assessed cells and coherent two-flank support. Each flank uses five cells separated by one guard cell. Report the 720 ms span centered on the nine centers with strongest deficit. Require strict positive over the development maximum of matched untouched, gain, genuine resampling and ordinary full-recording EQ controls.
method.roles: Reuse only the two previous source-panel development prompts for point selection. Select up to three held prompts from source readers not in any of the four earlier short-panel roles. Exclude the prior whole-utterance/ODSS readers and all exact old v9 source IDs. Use the publisher's matching word tier and the earlier source-duration, context and amplitude eligibility constraints. Prior speaker or training exposure is possible. Background captures and participants are disjoint from development.
method.scope: A temporary waveform change can result from ordinary editing or synthetic replacement. Count both as physical-change positives, with matched gain, resampling and EQ controls. Unrelated and same-text re-recorded references are admission controls. No model or customer scoring is used.
